html:
The copper mine at Falun in central Sweden was worked for about a thousand years, until 1992. In the 1600s it produced most of Europe's copper.

The Great Copper Mountain made Sweden's kings rich. Copper paid for the armies of Gustavus Adolphus in the Thirty Years' War, and Swedish copper money, including huge copper plates, was the coin of the realm. In 1687 the main workings collapsed into a great pit, which still gapes today, though no one was killed.

The mine also gave the world Falu red, the paint made from its waste that colours Swedish wooden houses. Its mining company, Stora, is one of the oldest companies in the world. Falun is a UNESCO World Heritage Site. See Sweden and its great power era.
